entities.summary: Euphuism is an elegant literary style that was briefly in fashion during the Elizabethan era. The euphuism style employed the frequent use of alliteration, antithesis, balance, and simile, with references to nature and mythological tales. Euphuism was fashionable in the 1580s, especially in the Elizabethan court. Its origins can be traced back to Spanish writer Antonio de Guevara, whose ornate, manierist courtesan prose became very popular throughout Europe, and whose work The Clock of the Princes, translated into English in 1557 by Thomas North, reached its peak in popularity during Elizabeth I's reign.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Euphuism's influence on Elizabethan literature and its ornate style can be seen in later writers such as Ben Jonson and John Donne. Although it was a brief fashion, euphuism contributed to the development of English literary language.
